main_text.p: 3 Plura hic latent adhuc mysteria. San-fon enim Christum significabat, [illegible, ~5 letters] illum iustitiæ, de quo Malach. 4. Is sponsam[?] ex gentibus sibi iunxit in matrimonium: rugientem leonem Satanam interfecit: victoriam de leone sponsæ suæ patefecit, &c. Huic igitur sit gloria in æternum, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XXI.
Pfalm. 127.

p.i: Anticum graduum Salome-nis: Si Dominus non ædificet domum, frustrà laborant qui ædificant eam: & si Do-minus non custodiat civitatem, frustrà vigilat custos. Vanum est vobis ut ma-turetis mane surgendo, & moram facia-tis sedendo, comedentes panem dolorum: sic dabit dilecto suo somnum. Ecce hæ-reditas Domini, filij sunt: & merces fru-ctus ventris. Sicut sagittæ in manu for-tis, sic sunt filij iuventutis. Beatus vir ille, qui ex his adimpleuit pharetram su-am: non pudefient, quando loquentur cum hostibus in porta.

main_text.p: {1} Titulus huius Psalmi est: Canticu Maa-loth.i. graduum, vel ascensionu, Salomonis

page.notes: The woodcut initial A of "Anticum" is decorative and joined to the word. The running head and page number are printed. "qu'a" at the start is a fragment; the mark over the a is uncertain. In verse 3, "San-fon" (Samson) is printed with a split at the line end and is read with uncertainty. The word before "illum" is unreadable. "sponsam" in the Samson passage is a conjecture: the scan reads "(ponam" and the word is uncertain. The long s is printed as f-like in the psalm and is transcribed as s. The footnote mark "1" is printed at the start of the footnote and is not visible in the psalm body.
